title: Lane lint on a stacked PR flags a head that does not hold its base branch's current head
why: A stacked PR can pass lane lint while it conflicts with its base's live head, because the lint reads the head against the base and never checks that the head holds the base's head. The conflict surfaces only at batch release.
note: Incident (lane bg-tail-loses-verdict, session_013NEJL3ZjZdzrS8tBezxY85, 02:20 CST Nov 9): the same docstring edit was made separately on three stacked branches (#2015, #2091, #2156) instead of on the bottom branch and merged up. The wrapping differed, so #2156 conflicted with #2015's live head; the coordinator caught it at release. Candidate: `merge --lane-lint <pr>` on a stacked PR refuses, or warns, when the head does not contain its base branch's current head, or when `git merge-tree` against the base conflicts. Refuse or warn: the lane decides from the false-alarm cost.
